jobs.description: Company description:Ericsson ABJob description:   Join our Team   About this opportunity: Are you passionate about driving innovation and working on groundbreaking 5G and 6G mobile communication solutions? Do you thrive in a flexible working culture, where new insights are championed, and you are encouraged to develop new skills? Then join Ericsson and our team in Stockholm, Sweden.  We are looking for an FPGA Developer within the Ericsson Silicon organization. You will work with dedicated engineers passionate about developing world-class Radio and RAN Compute products. You will contribute to the FPGA team by developing and integrating high-performance FPGA solutions.  As part of our global organization, you'll collaborate with talented teams across our different sites. We are committed to Agile principles, fostering a collaborative and innovative work environment that encourages creativity and teamwork.    What you will do:      Design and implement FPGA-based Radio and RAN Compute solutions.        Develop and optimize FPGA designs for performance, power and cost-efficiency.        Apply industry-standard tools and methodologies for FPGA development and implementation.        Stay up to date with relevant FPGA technologies, tools and development methods.        Document design specifications, test procedures and results.        Participate in design reviews and contribute ideas to improve FPGA solutions.        Develop testbenches and test cases for your FPGA designs, following functional specifications, agreed verification plans and Ericsson development processes.        Use functional and code coverage results to identify verification gaps and meet agreed coverage targets.        Debug RTL issues found in simulation and on hardware, together with other designers.        Collaborate with hardware, software, systems and integration teams across Radio and RAN Compute development to understand product requirements and contribute to efficient solutions.        Contribute to the continuous improvement of products, tools and processes.     The skills you bring:      A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering or equivalent.        3–5 years of experience in FPGA/ASIC development, including RTL design and verification.        Solid knowledge of FPGA technology, design environment and methodology.        Hands-on use of FPGA design tools (e.g., Vivado, Quartus, or similar).        Proficiency in a hardware description language (HDL) such as Verilog or VHDL.        Working knowledge of interfaces and protocols such as DDR, AXI4, PCIe, SPI or I2C.        Scripting skills, for example in Python, Tcl or shell scripting.        Ability to create RTL testbenches to verify your own designs.        Familiarity with hardware architecture and digital signal processing.        Knowledge of SystemVerilog and UVM experience is a plus.        An analytical, results-oriented approach with the ability to manage priorities and meet agreed commitments.        Good English spoken and written communication skills.        Self-motivation and the ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with others.        Experience collaborating across teams and sites.

Company description:Epiroc is a leading productivity partner for the mining, infrastructure and natural resources industries. Withcutting-edge technology, Epiroc develops and produces innovative drill rigs, rock excavation and constructionequipment, and provides world-class service and consumables. The company was founded in Stockholm,Sweden, and has passionate people supporting and collaborating with customers in more than 150 countries.Learn more at www.epirocgroup.com.Job description:We’re looking for a Product Owner – AI & Test Engineering to join our SW Platform organization. We’re responsible for the machine platform that Epiroc’s mining and construction equipment runs on. In this role, AI is at the heart of what you do. You’ll help shape how software developers across all of Epiroc use AI in their daily work, and how AI changes the way we test and verify our software. Are you curious about how AI is changing software development? Do you enjoy collaborating with people across teams and helping turn needs into clear priorities? Would you like to help build something new from the start, with an impact across the whole company? Then we’d love to hear from you. A stream in the making AI & Test Engineering is a new product stream in our platform organisation. The teams are being built right now, and their setup, size and exact scope aren’t finalised yet. As Product Owner, you’ll have a real opportunity to influence how the stream takes shape, together with the teams, your manager and the Chief Product Owner. Your mission As Product Owner you’re responsible for the AI & Test Engineering product stream, where AI is the main focus. The stream is planned to cover two areas:      AI Software Factory: exploring and introducing AI-supported, agentic ways of working across the software development lifecycle, for all software developers at Epiroc.     AI-driven Test & Integration: using AI to rethink how we test and integrate platform software, together with test frameworks, simulation, a software-defined lab and system testing.  You connect the teams with their stakeholders. For the AI Software Factory, these are software developers and development teams across Epiroc’s divisions and sites. For Test & Integration, they are mainly the internal teams that develop and deliver on the platform. You’re responsible for the product backlog in Jira and the roadmap. By listening to stakeholders and understanding their needs, you help translate them into clear epics and user stories and support the teams in focusing on what creates the most value. You keep up with how AI in software development is evolving and help turn new possibilities into practical value for developers and testers. You work closely with the Scrum Masters and Tech Leads, collaborate with our architects and work closely with the Chief Product Owner on the overall platform roadmap. You also take part in cross-team planning together with the other product streams. You’ll report to a team manager in the SW Platform organization and be part of a supportive team where knowledge sharing and learning are encouraged.Profile description:Your profile      You have experience as a Product Owner or in a similar role, for example product manager, test lead, technical project lead or requirements owner, in a software development environment.     You have a genuine interest in AI and how it can support software development and testing, and you may already use AI tools in your own work.     You’re familiar with agile ways of working such as Scrum and with tools like Jira.     You enjoy working with a broad range of stakeholders and helping new ways of working spread across an organization.     It’s a plus if you have experience with AI-assisted or agentic software development, AI in testing, test automation, CI/CD or simulation.     You speak Swedish and you’re fluent in English, both written and spoken.  As a person, you’re curious, structured, communicative and collaborative. You’re comfortable when not everything is decided yet, and you enjoy helping to create structure together with others. You build trusting relationships with stakeholders, help the teams find focus and like to keep learning. We know that great candidates don’t always meet every requirement. If this role sounds interesting, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We welcome applicants of all genders and backgrounds and believe diverse teams build better products. Location The role is based in Örebro, Sweden. We work hybrid, with at least three days a week in the office. Application and contacts Please send your application, including CV and personal letter, by creating an account in our recruitment system as soon as possible but no later than 27th of November. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before last application date. Please note that, due to the current regulations, we will only consider applications received through our system and not via email or social media.

Working at both an architectural and technical level, you help transform future needs into scalable, user-friendly solutions. Participate in the MES architecture forum and establish shared development principles with fellow architects.     Shape modern solutions using C#, Angular, OAuth 2.0, Kubernetes, pipelines and DevOps practices.     Guide development teams through design reviews, code reviews and technical coaching. Do you enjoy creating clarity at the intersection of customers, Sales and Supply Chain? We’re looking for a Supply Chain Sales Support Manager to lead our global function and develop a proactive, structured and data-driven service that colleagues and customers can rely on.  At Seco, collaboration, responsibility, curiosity and continuous improvement guide how we work and grow. Here, you get to:     Lead a global function at the heart of customer order flow.     Shape how Sales and Supply Chain work together through clear governance, service levels, KPIs and digital tools.     Join a collaborative environment where curiosity and continuous learning are valued.   About the job  You lead and develop the global Supply Chain Sales Support function, creating a standardized, customer-focused and efficient interface between Sales and our end-to-end supply chain. With a clear focus on governance and proactive support, you ensure that customer needs, order exceptions and supply constraints are translated into priorities and coordinated action.  The function is in the middle of a shift: building on a strong foundation in case handling towards an end-to-end control and improvement capability. You lead that change, and you lead it through people. Developing your team’s skills, ownership and confidence is as much a part of the job as the processes and tools.  Job responsibilities     Lead, coach and develop the Supply Chain Sales Support team: set clear roles and expectations, build capability in customer communication, supply chain understanding, problem-solving and case management, and grow people into broader ownership.     Lead the development towards proactive exception management, building on the team’s case-handling expertise, and make new ways of working stick in daily operations.     Establish and maintain global governance across the order-to-delivery flow, including ownership boundaries, decision rights and escalation paths.     Act as the primary supply chain interface for Sales and Customer Service regarding prioritized orders, supply exceptions and special customer requirements.     Develop the service model, including case categories, service levels, prioritization principles, escalation protocols and KPIs.     Use case data and performance insights to identify root causes and drive structural improvements with the responsible process owners.     Drive digitalization of case management, workflows, reporting and knowledge management, reducing repetitive demand through automation and self-service.  Location and flexibility  The position is flexible is preferably based in Fagersta, Sweden, but another Seco location can be considered for the right candidate. We offer a hybrid working model that combines time at the office with remote work.  Your profile   You have solid experience in supply chain, logistics, planning, order management or customer service operations. Having worked at the intersection of a commercial organization and operational supply chain functions, you’re comfortable creating structure across complex, cross-functional environments and using data to support decisions. You communicate fluently in English; Swedish is considered an advantage.  Your background includes:      Experience establishing processes, ownership models, escalation paths or service frameworks across multiple functions.     Knowledge of customer-order exceptions, escalations and prioritization, preferably within a case-based way of working.     The ability to identify recurring operational issues, uncover root causes and turn insights into structural improvements.     Experience using CRM or case-management systems, ERP data, KPIs and reporting.     People leadership experience and a university degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Industrial Engineering or equivalent experience. Customer focus and structure are central to your way of working. You simplify complex supply chain situations, create a shared understanding among commercial and operational colleagues and distinguish individual exceptions from structural problems. Calm and solution-focused, you challenge unnecessary manual work and fragmented processes while moving issues confidently towards resolution. The teamYou lead the global Supply Chain Sales Support team and work closely with Sales, Customer Service, Planning, Logistics, Production Units, Distribution Centres, IT and other operational functions. Together, you create globally consistent ways of working while accommodating relevant local requirements. Our Seco culture   At Seco, we're united by a spirit of collaboration and a shared curiosity to learn and grow. jobs.occupation: Head Chef, Aurora Mountain Lodge, Lannavaara, Sweden
jobs.description: We are looking for a Head Chef for the winter season at the beautiful Aurora Mountain Lodge.This is the place for you if you want to combine professional kitchen work with the peace of Arctic nature.Aurora Mountain Lodge is located in the small village of Lannavaara, by the Lainio River, about 200 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle in Northern Sweden. Only 73 people live in the village year-round. The lodge is surrounded by stunning open landscapes and reindeer herding land, with Kuormakka fell rising in the distance.The lodges cozy restaurant serves delicious food made from local ingredients.Guests can enjoy breakfast and lunch buffets and 3-course dinner meals as well as a small, high-quality à la carte menu.In this role, you will be responsible for the day-to-day running of the kitchen and lead the kitchen team. You will also take an active part in cooking alongside your team. The concept and menus are already in place, so you can get started quickly and focus on delivering high quality.The position starts as soon as the right person is found, in late November, and lasts until the end of the winter season, around 15 April 2027.We hope you have- experience as a chef and in a kitchen leadership role- good organisational and leadership skills, and enthusiasm for working alongside your team- good English skills, as English is the working language- a love of nature and a peaceful environmentWe offer- a full-time position, around 40 hours per week, with regular working hours- time to enjoy your free time in stunning natural surroundings- a friendly, international team- accommodation right next to the workplace at a reasonable rent- a unique winter season in Swedish Lapland- good staff benefits, for example staff can join safari tours for free and can borrow gear for freeApply now!The recruitment is carried out together with Nordic Career, and the selected person will be employed directly by Aurora Mountain Lodge.Send your application and CV through our application system.The position starts soon, so we will interview candidates during the application period.For more information about the position, please contact Nordic Career:Heidi-Maria Viitanen, tel. +358 50 479 7570, heidi-maria.viitanen@career.fiLinda Hämäläinen, tel. +358 50 532 3775, linda.hamalainen@career.fiNordic Career~ Nordic Career on lappilainen henkilöstöpalvelualan yritys, joka on osa Career.fi henkilöstötaloa.Teemme työmme sydämellä, kunnioittaen arvojamme, välittäminen, kiltteys, ilo, rohkeus, vastuullisuus ja oppiminen. Etsitään yhdessä sinulle työ, jota on ilo tehdä! ~Phone: +358505482448 Email: minna.mantovaara@career.fi Location: Guldvaskarvägen 4 SE-985 93 Lannavaara, Sweden

We are looking for a dedicated Imaging Engineer to strengthen our team! In this role you will further develop the imaging platform for our production systems but also support industrialization and R&D to turn new products and ideas into mass production. Does this sound interesting? Keep reading and welcome with your application!Who is your future team?You will join the Imaging team, a specialized group of four experienced engineers focused on developing the imaging parts needed within our production systems to produce Axis cameras with high image quality.These production systems play a critical role in supporting high-volume manufacturing operations at our global facilities, where millions of products are produced and tested annually.The Imaging team is part of a larger division of about 60+ engineers working with Production Engineering and Technology (PET), and together with our colleagues within SW, electronics and mechanical engineering we develop and maintain production systems globally.What you'll do here as Imaging EngineerAs an Imaging Engineer, you'll contribute to the design, development and maintenance of imaging production tests that enable the testing of Axis products in our production systems. You will also be a part of our development projects where we use innovative imaging and optical solutions to design efficient and reliable production systems.Typical tasks include handling topics related to optics, collimators and other imaging equipment needed to produce Axis' products.You will also play an important role in designing, developing, and maintaining software frameworks used for verification and calibration of our production systems. This includes collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless production processes.Key responsibilities include:    Designing and maintaining both SW and HW for the imaging tests framework to support production processes.    Developing and maintaining software frameworks to facilitate machine monitoring, verification, calibration and production testing using C# and Python    Providing technical support to R&D product development initiatives    Analyzing production data to drive system improvements and innovation    Contributing to strategic planning for future imaging test developmentOur team leverages a range of technologies, including:    Hardware like different types of optics and collimators    Programming languages: C#, Python, C++    Tools: Jira, Confluence, QlikView, Visual Studio, GitHub Copilot    Version control systems: Git, SVN, Gerrit    Continuous integration platforms: TeamCity    Agile methodologiesWho are we looking for/Who are you?We think you are a dedicated engineer with skills in imaging, optics and software development who is curious, responsible, organized and methodical. You enjoy problem solving and working with both hardware and software. Ability to communicate is important as the role requires collaboration with other teams and departments. The work includes a lot of freedom and independence, which requires that you are proactive and take initiative.We'd love to hear that you have:    Experience within optics, collimators or other imaging equipment    A huge interest in software development and optics    Finding solutions to complex technical problems    Interest in the complexity of production and creating efficient production systems for our factories around the world    University degree preferably within computer science, engineering, physics, electrical engineering or equivalent    At least a couple of years of experience from roles in a development organization    Good communication skills in English and Swedish, both in speech and writingThe position is full time. Travelling is not required, but there will probably be possibilities to visit our factories around the world.What Axis has to offerWe are a world leader in network video, where cutting-edge technology meets global impact. Here, you'll contribute to meaningful projects that shape the future of security and surveillance - developing solutions used worldwide.As a fast-growing company, we offer exciting career opportunities. You'll grow professionally through continuous learning, supported by a collaborative team that values creativity, innovation, and work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us. We offer a range of benefits, including a company bonus, Friday cake, wellness allowance, health insurance - and even your own Axis bicycle.To learn more about Axis, our innovative products, solutions, and vibrant company culture, explore:Life at Axis blogEngineering at Axis blogInnovation at AxisReady to Act?Axis is a company realizing the benefits of a diverse workforce. We know that diversity in groups creates a better working environment and promotes creativity, something that is fundamental for our success. We welcome all applications. We go through applications continuously so don't wait - send in your application today!In case of questions, please reach out to recruiting manager Michael Rosenberg at +46 46 272 1800

jobs.occupation: Associate researcher in Experimental lung transplantation
jobs.description: Description of workplaceThe research group is led by Associated professor Sandra Lindstedt and has a long-standing interest in research related to lung transplantation, post-transplant complications, and lung regeneration. The group focuses on developing novel therapeutic strategies to treat lung injury, improve donor organ quality, and reduce complications following lung transplantation. A particular focus is on acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and regenerative approaches to lung repair.We offerLund University is a governmental authority, which means you get special benefits, generous holidays, and a favorable occupational pension. Read more on the university's website about being employed at Lund University, Work at Lund UniversityWork descriptionA associate researcher position is available within the Lindstedt research group, focusing on translational research in lung transplantation, lung injury, and regenerative medicine. The duties at the research unit primarily consist of experimental and laboratory-based research, with a particular focus on the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies to improve lung repair and transplantation outcomes.The main responsibilities include:    independently designing, planning, coordinating, and conducting research projects, as well as collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and managing experimental data.    The work involves the development and optimization of experimental protocols, evaluation of therapeutic interventions, and application of cellular, molecular, ultra-high-plexed immunofluorescence and histological techniques to investigate mechanisms of lung injury, repair, and regeneration.    The position also includes responsibility for preparing high-quality scientific manuscripts for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, contributing to research grant applications, and presenting research findings at national and international scientific conferences.    The majority of the work will be conducted independently, while also involving close collaboration with internal and external research partners and clinical collaborators.    In addition, the position includes mentorship and supervision of doctoral students, Bachelor’s and Master’s students, and other junior researchers, as well as contributing to the coordination and development of ongoing research activities within the group.Other work tasks might also be included.QualificationsRequired qualifications    PhD (or equivalent) in biomedical sciences, biotechnology, molecular biology, regenerative medicine, or a related field.    A minimum of four years of documented research experience following completion of the PhD, demonstrating scientific independence and responsibility.    Documented experience in experimental and translational biomedical research, particularly within cell therapies, lung injury, lung transplantation, or regenerative medicine.    Hands-on experience with small and large-animal models and/or ex vivo organ perfusion.    Experience with standard cellular and molecular biology techniques, including cell culture, ELISA, Western blotting, qPCR, immunohistochemistry and high-plexed immunofluorescence.    Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, coordinate, and conduct complex experimental research projects.    Documented scientific productivity through publications in international peer-reviewed journals.    Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.    Independent and responsible, with the ability to organize and manage research activities and take responsibility for scientific quality and project progress.    Collaborative, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary research environments.    Analytical and solution-oriented, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and address complex scientific challenges.Meritorious qualifications:    Additional specialized training in experimental transplantation, regenerative medicine, cell therapy, or related disciplines.    Relevant training and certification in laboratory animal science, particularly involving large- and small-animal experimental models.    Completed courses in higher education teaching and pedagogy.    Experience with experimental lung transplantation, including large- and small-animal models of lung injury and transplantation.    Hands-on experience with ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) and human ex vivo lung models, including precision-cut lung slices (PCLS).    Experience in the development and evaluation of cell-based and regenerative therapies, particularly mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and mitochondrial therapeutics.    Experience with cellular, molecular, histological, and proteomic analyses, including the handling and processing of human and animal tissue samples.    Experience in managing and coordinating interdisciplinary research projects and national or international collaborations.    Documented experience in scientific supervision, preparation of research grant applications, and dissemination of research findings through publications and international conferences.Other informationThe position is a fixed-term employment according to the Special Fixed-term Employment (SÄVA) regulations §5 p1 LAS, and it is full-time. Department of Biosystems and TechnologyPhD Project: Valorization and Risk Assessment of Anaerobic Digestates for Sustainable Horticultural ProductionThird-cycle subject area: Horticultural ScienceDescription of the doctoral project The transition to circular food and energy systems requires safe, high-quality products that can return nutrients and organic matter to horticultural production. Anaerobic digestate from biogas production is a promising resource containing plant nutrients and organic fibre originating from, for example, manure, food and household waste, slaughterhouse by-products, park and garden residues, and biomass from intermediate crops or roadside vegetation. The digestate can be separated into a nutrient-rich liquid fraction and a fibre fraction. While the liquid fraction has potential for use in nutrient solutions, the fibre fraction is particularly relevant as a constituent of growing media and a potential partial replacement for peat and other fibre materials. Developing safe, functional and locally available alternatives to peat is an important challenge for sustainable horticultural production. A key barrier is the possible presence of pyralid herbicide residues. These herbicides can accumulate in crop material, persist during anaerobic digestion and cause growth disturbances in sensitive horticultural crops at very low concentrations. The project will investigate the occurrence and fate of pyralids in selected feedstocks and digestate fractions, with particular focus on the fibre fraction and its use in growing media.About the positionThe doctoral project will combine greenhouse and growth-chamber bioassays with laboratory studies and chemical characterisation. It will assess effects on plant growth and nutrient uptake, examine the distribution, degradation and immobilisation of herbicide residues, and generate knowledge to support risk assessment and the safe valorisation of digestate-derived growing-media products. The project is an important part in the ongoing transition for more circular productions systems where plant nutrients and fiber is recycled from waste to production. The project is a part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center, which means that there will be collaboration with other PhD students both at SLU and at Linköping University. Communication of results, both orally and in writing to both academic and industrial stakeholders are also important parts of the project. As a PhD-student, you will also take PhD courses and be a part of the daily work at the department.RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in Horticultural Science. To meet the specific entry requirements the applicant must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.You should have received a degree at advanced level (second cycle) within the fields of Horticultural Science, Agricultural Science, or similar subject. You should also have documented experience with laboratory work and experimental work within the field of study.Beneficial competences Driver’s licence valid in Sweden. Documented experience from scientific writing and scientific communication.Your profileWe are looking for an engaged and self-going candidate with genuine interest in horticulture and circular solutions. Suitable backgrounds are as a Horticulturist or Agronomist. Experience with laboratory work, for example microbial analyses, is beneficial. You should also have experience with practical plant cultivation. Great emphasis will be put on personal skills like curiosity, ability to work individually and in group, and ability to independently plan and perform research related tasks. You are expected to be open to new challenges and to take on various work tasks to contribute to the development of the department’s activities. Very good skills in speaking and writing in English is mandatory.About usAt the department of Biosystems and Technology you will work in a multi-disciplinary environment together with around 60 colleagues, among which around 10 PhD students. The holder of this position will be a part of a national, transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities (Linköping University and SLU) and about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system and has additional support from Swedish Energy Agency. All doctoral positions advertised within BSRC will be formulated so that they fit into the competence center's research plans and at the same time reflect our parties' interests. This way, we ensure long-term competence supply to both industry and academia.Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/Form of employment / Funding Employment as a doctoral student (4-year programme). jobs.occupation: PhD student in agricultural bioeconomy systems
jobs.description: Department of Biosystems and TechnologyPhD project: Sustainable utilisation of agricultural green biomass in integrated protein and biogas systemsSubject area: TechnologyDescription of the doctoral project A circular and fossil-independent bioeconomy requires renewable biomass without increasing competition for agricultural land and food production. Crop residues and intermediate crops are therefore particularly relevant resources. Research at SLU shows that these biomass resources can be substantial, but their potential and sustainable utilisation vary regionally. They can be used for biogas, while effects on soil carbon and nutrient cycling need to be considered.  Green biomass can also be biorefined into plant protein for feed or food, after which the remaining streams are used for biogas. The same feedstock can thereby provide protein, energy and recycled nutrients.The project aims to assess the potential and consequences of large-scale utilisation of green crop residues and intermediate crops in integrated biogas and green biorefinery systems.The project will:    assess sustainably available biomass from green crop residues and intermediate crops in Sweden;    assess the potential for biogas and combined plant protein and biogas production;    develop implementation scenarios based on feedstock availability, infrastructure, logistics and markets;    assess effects on nutrient cycling, soil carbon, biomethane, fertilizer use, and feed and food production; and    evaluate economic and wider socio-economic benefits, drawbacks and trade-offs.The project combines GIS and agricultural data with mass and nutrient balances, scenario modelling, and life cycle-based, techno-economic and socio-economic methods. Data will be drawn from research, statistics, literature and national databases.The doctoral student will join an interdisciplinary research environment at SLU Alnarp focusing on sustainable agricultural production, bioenergy, circular bioeconomy and systems analysis.About the positionThe work includes collection and processing of agricultural and process data, GIS, modelling of biomass and product flows, scenario development, and environmental and economic assessments.  You will integrate information from crop production and biomass availability to biorefineries, biogas, and food and energy systems.  You will analyse data, develop models and scenarios, and publish and present research results. The work will be conducted with researchers at SLU and external partners.  The doctoral student will be part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC), a national transdisciplinary centre where Linköping University, SLU and around 50 private and public organisations collaborate. The centre is supported by the Swedish Energy Agency. The PhD project follows BSRC’s research plans and contributes to long-term competence development in industry and academia.RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in technology. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.  You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.You should have a Master’s degree or equivalent in, for example, biosystems/agricultural engineering, environmental engineering, agricultural science, energy systems, industrial ecology, environmental science or a related field.Your profileWe are looking for a motivated candidate interested in sustainable agricultural and bioeconomy systems and quantitative analysis.Experience or documented knowledge in one or several of the following areas is desirable:    systems analysis, modelling or scenario analysis;    GIS and spatial analysis;    life cycle assessment, environmental systems analysis or material-flow analysis;    techno-economic or socio-economic assessment;    bioenergy, biogas or biorefinery systems;    agricultural production systems and agricultural biomass;    statistical analysis and handling of larger datasets;    experience of programming or quantitative modelling, for example using Python, R or MATLAB.You should have good analytical skills, be able to integrate information from different fields, work independently and collaborate well.Excellent written and spoken English is required. Good communication skills are important. Knowledge of Swedish is advantageous but not required.Personal qualities, motivation and the ability to successfully complete doctoral studies will be given considerable weight. We have the power of over 50,000 students and co-workers. Students who provide hope for the future. Co-workers who contribute to Linköping University meeting challenges of today. Our fundamental values rest on credibility, trust and security. By having the courage to think freely and innovate, our actions together, large and small, contribute to a better world. We look forward to receiving your application! Are you interested in the potential of citizens' assemblies and other democratic innovations to drive climate transformation? Come join us!Work assignments The Environmental Change division (tema Miljöförändring) at the Department of Thematic Studies is looking to hire a two-year postdoctoral researcher specializing in democratic innovations.You will be part of the Formas-funded research project Democratic Innovations for Climate Transformation (2027-2029), which entails a systematic and interdisciplinary knowledge synthesis of how climate citizens’ assemblies and related democratic processes can contribute to system transformation. The project explores what the existing research literature tells us about the political impact of climate assemblies, how they might contribute to broader systemic transformations, and what this means for Swedish climate governance.As postdoc on the project, you will take a leading role in carrying out the systematic literature review across academic databases and grey literature, following established standards for searching, screening, and quality assessment. You will contribute centrally to the comparative synthesis of findings across studies, and to identifying evidence gaps in how deliberative processes connect to system-level transformation. You will also help design and facilitate stakeholder dialogues with Swedish municipalities and practitioners, which ensures that the resulting knowledge is robust and genuinely useful for policy and practice.You will work in close collaboration with the project’s principal investigator and a research team from LiU and Stockholm Resilience Centre. There is considerable room to help shape the project’s methodological choices and analytical framework, and to co-author academic outputs arising from the review and synthesis work.As postdoc, you will principally carry out research. A certain amount of teaching may be part of your duties, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.QualificationsTo be qualified to take employment as postdoc, you must have been awarded a doctoral degree or have a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree. This degree must have been awarded at the latest by the point at which LiU makes its decision to employ you.Your doctoral degree should preferably have been awarded no more than three years ago. If there are special reasons, a degree awarded more than three years ago may be accepted. Special reasons include sick leave, parental leave, trade union positions of trust, service in the defense, or other similar circumstances, as well as service or assignments relevant to the subject area.We are looking for someone with a doctoral degree in social sciences, humanities, or related fields, and a demonstrated familiarity with the research area of democratic innovations – for example, deliberative democracy, citizens’ assemblies, participatory governance, or environmental/climate governance. Experience carrying out systematic literature reviews and others forms of qualitative content analysis is considered a merit. So is prior experience with stakeholder involvement and co-production through workshops and similar formats.You are curious, rigorous, and comfortable moving between the fine-grained work of systematic screening and coding and the bigger-picture task of synthesizing what it all means. You enjoy working collaboratively, taking initiative, and are able to communicate complex research to non-academic audiences, such as policymakers and practitioners. A strong command of written and spoken English is required.The workplaceYou will be employed at the Department of Thematic Studies where you will be affiliated with the Environmental Change theme. You can read about the workplace https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/tema/temam.The employmentThis employment is a temporary full-time contract of two years. Starting date is Januari 1, 2027, or as soon as possible.
